TextEng: This helm mounts two special crystal lenses over the wearer's eyes that grant a +5 bonus to Spot checks.

This metallurgist's helm bears the distinctive look of gnomish make.  It has been specially constructed to allow an intricate series of lenses to swivel over the wearer's eyes. They enable much improved close-range vision and are very useful for locating or identifying features such as tiny seams, marks, cracks, or imperfections.

This helm mounts two lenses of dark crystal over the wearer's eyes. Even though the lenses are opaque, when placed over the eyes of the wearer they enable normal sight and also grant darkvision.

Common equipment for adventurers who like to explore deep caves and underground ruins, these helms are also hailed as "the great equalizer" by humans and are quite popular among human rogues.

Woven round the brim of this helm is a light cord with a small gem set so that it rests upon the forehead of the wearer.  The magic of the headband has the power to dramatically sharpen the wearer's intellect.

The god Callahi expects his followers to have "honey-tongues" when dealing with others. For those who do not come by this naturally, there are always magical enhancments. While many consider such enhancements to be mere vanity, many merchants will swear that they have doubled their profits with said assistance.

Forged by clerics of Suhili, the sun goddess, these shields are constantly aglow with the golden fires of the sun. Depending on the skill and intent of the crafter, some Shields of the Sun carry more potent powers as well.

The lesser robe of eyes, like its more powerful counterpart, provides the wearer with improved vision and the ability to detect many things that are hidden. Once per day, the wearer can invoke the power of the robe to pierce the veil of invisibility or etherealness.

This is a very heavy helmet, made from a dense, durable metal. A small inscription on the inside of the helm says, "Made in Stettler". You've never heard of such a place, but it is most likely some lost civilization.

This simple rope belt, when wrapped around a person's waist, confers increased ability in unarmed combat.  

When the Shining Moon order of monks were attacked by a rival order, it was necessary for some of the apprentices to rise more rapidly than they normally could. These belts allowed the younger monks to defend their order with great speed and skill.

Near the end of the Age of the Magi, legends tell that the first Emporer of Valratha used hunters who seemed to resist many of the spells used by their victims. By the end of his rule, the Emporer had destroyed the majority of mages across Valratha. Even today, mages of any power are few and far between.

An unusual tradition in the mountainous village of Kale sprang up around 5 years ago, where villagers would take blunted arrows and fire them at each other in contests. Two lines would form up, with each person directly across from the other firing on command. Anyone not hit would remain, while all others backed out, until one person was left standing.
Travellers to the village reported the games were, "Marvellous fun to watch, but you'd have to be a bloody idiot to participate."
After a few years and several unfortunate deaths, the villagers went back to shooting at stuffed targets.

Attempting to form an anti-thieves' guild, Ronger Delphos, a successful merchant, paid thieves to become security experts. The guards were trained to use wands with the Hold Person spell, to capture the thieves for interrogation. To counteract this security measure, magical belts were purchased by the thieves' guild, which nullified the effects of such spells. In the escalating war between the two guilds, many of these belts found their way into pawnshops and equipment stores.

Blessed by priests of Calahi the god of merchants and travel, these boots seem to make even the most arduous journey easier and more pleasant. This is accomplished not by increasing the wearer's speed, but by making him hardier and more resistant to pain. Numerous versions of these boots exist, their power varying largely in accordance with the priest who blessed them.

The Tumblers were a group of assassins who worked together to topple rich, powerful nobles and merchants. Emperor Fenias IV used them to regain control over the various provinces of Valratha, whose nobles had become almost entirely independent of the crown.

While these magical items have been around for thousands of years, their popularity never seems to decrease. Recently, a party of adventurers out of Delish uncovered a vast treasure trove, filled with magical items like these. The sudden influx of magical gauntlets does not seem to have decreased their value, as every adventurer across the land clamors for the assistance of these useful artifacts.

The elderly priestess, Milladolin, found that age was affecting her and her fellows quite rapidly, causing their hands to shake and preventing them from performing many of their priestly duties. With Rictos's blessings, Milladolin created magical gloves that steadied their hands and heightened their muscle control. Years later, a young Rictosian was caught for thievery - guilty of using the gloves. Word spread, and soon the gloves themselves were stolen away.
The gloves are covered with small copper rivets.  The wearer may use the gloves to throw a sharp electric jolt at a nearby target.

Monks of this Order frequently travel alongside paladins of Jaess, serving as trusted guides and companions to these knights of the servant lord.

When Jacin Maltis, a petty lord in Sembia, paid for the crafting of an amulet to increase his health, he expected a tasteful necklace with a small, but precious gem mounted in it. When he placed the necklace around his neck and the diamond turned a gaudy blood red, he refused to pay the wizard who created it. The wizard simply smiled, and loosed a spell that instantly destroyed the noble. Copies of this amulet were found circulating months later in the distant city of Waterdeep.

Understanding his pain but unable to identify any specific demonic influence, the church tried crafting rings that they hoped would clear his thoughts. Unfortunately, while the rings enhanced his senses they did nothing for the voices, and Resino eventually took his own life.

Samile the Nervous was a golddigger known for surviving the betrayal of at least five partners. He always seemed to be aware of what was going on, seconds before anyone else did. After the trouble with the Kobold colony began in the Emerald Hills, the farmers requested assistance from the Keep's militia. The Keep, however, was under a near constant state of siege and no guards could be spared to clean out the caves. The farmers who lived near the area could not deal with the Kobolds directly due to their lack of experience. They instead created a pen around the caves to hold the creatures in. This unfortunately had little effect on the Kobold horde as they simply climbed the wall. In the end, the farmers left the pen sealed to keep wanderers from meeting their doom within the caves.

A long time ago there was an ivory tower in the Emerald Hills which housed a wizard's academy. The school thrived for many generations until the headmaster passed away. Soon after, the lesser instructors of the school began squabbling over control of the academy. As the bickering and scheming of the instructors became more belligerent, the size of the faculty decreased until only two instructors remained. In the final battle for control of the school, the two instructors destroyed one another, taking the upper levels of the academy with them. Only the subterranean level, where the creatures used for making the academy's famed magical items were held, survived unscathed.

This is the journal of the last lord of the keep's advisor. It seems to be largely intact and mostly boring until near the end. These are a few interesting excerpts:
"My Lord has become more and more obsessed with the idea of controlling an undead army. He has the key I found that will open the planar gate, yet I fear that we are missing something... something very important. I have found some oblique references to another key, but I know not what the other key would do, nor where it lies. I shall have to return to the ruins and see if I can finally discover a way to activate the crystal ball. I am sure the answers must be hidden within it."
The last entry:
"My lord is impatient to open the planar gate. I have begged him to hold off until I am done here, and my efforts have finally paid off. Today I managed to activate the crystal ball! The second key is used for controlling the undead army. Without it, opening the planar gate would be suicide! I can now return and tell my lord exactly where the second key is and how it works. I am sure he will be pleased with... now where did my page run off to? There was a noise in the antechamber, which I sent him to investigate, but he hasn't returned. I guess I shall have to go find him, then return to the keep."

Desperately seeking to escape the attention of the emporer's assassins, the wizard, Worlit Thent fled to the fey hidden lands, Kahnahda. Peace and beauty are exalted above all else in these lands, so the emporer's assassins were unable to enter. When Worlit decided it was time to leave, the fey gave him an unprecidented gift. The feyduster was a weapon of beauty, but still a weapon. The fairy who gave it to Worlit told him it was from an age when the fey lived more in the world and made war on the big folk.
